parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
For many parts of the world today, a lack of clean drinking water is a major problem. In some developing areas, bore water, which is water that comes out of the ground, is the only water available. Unfortunately, bore water may be dangerous to drink because it contains excessive amounts of salts. In recent months, I’ve been working with a research team to develop a device that will help solve this problem. What we came up with is a solar water purifier, which we have called the SW40. And this device not only makes bore water drinkable, it can even process sea water in fact, it even passed the rigorous testing standards applied by hospitals to determine whether water is sterile enough for use there. The only problem we do face at the moment is with its manufacturing. The present method involves a process called vacuum forming which tends to be rather slow. We’d like to change to an injection mode of process, which is much faster, but would cost quite a lot to switch to, around 1 million Australian dollars. There are a number of private companies that are very keen to go into partnership with us over this. What my preferred option would be a global aid agency known as Health International that sponsors projects like ours. It has a long history of working in these areas, and although it may take a little longer to get an agreement, it should mean a better deal all around. So just how useful is this device of ours? Well, the amount of pure water it is capable of producing each day varies as the amount of sunlight available varies. However, on a hot day when the temperature is around about 25 to 30 degrees Celsius, with the sun shining clearly through a blue sky, it produces anywhere from 7 liters per day to as much as 9 liters. Now, most people can survive on 1 to 2 liters per day. So even under difficult conditions, one family could live off one of these devices. So a normal size village would require several of these to supply all its needs.

Okay, so let’s look at the device in more detail. It weighs 8 kilograms and is the size of a medium sized suitcase. The SW40 has no filters, no electronics, no moving parts, and uses no chemicals. So how does it work? Well, there’s a rectangular box with a glass lid on it, and on the edge of the box is a steel frame to hold everything together. And inside the box is a piece of black plastic which is divided up into pockets. You need an incline so the water flows through the device. The optimum is 12.5 degrees to the horizontal, although it can be 1 or 2 degrees above or below that. Impure water is piped in at the top of the box and flows down through the little pockets until they’re all full. You then let mother nature in the form of the sun do its work as it shines through the glass window. It produces infra red light which heats the water. At the same time ultraviolet light from the sun or UV as we more commonly call it is also radiated. If there are germs present in the water, prolonged exposure to this type of light will kill them. Then, as the temperature of the water rises due to the sun’s heat, the water vaporizes and condenses on the underside of the glass panel. The droplets of water slowly run down the glass to a collection tank, ready to be taken away for drinking or whatever. So that’s basically how it works. Now, what this means?

analyses.content: 录音中提到地下水（bore water）可能很危险，因为它包含过量的 salts（盐分），对应题目 make... unsafe to drink。
Unfortunately, bore water may be dangerous to drink because it contains excessive amounts of salts.
不要被 dangerous 这个形容词干扰，题目问的是造成危险的“物质”是什么；虽然录音说的是 salts（复数），但填空时若题目语境不可数，填 salt 也是通用的。
...it even passed the rigorous testing standards applied by hospitals to determine whether water is sterile enough for use there.
不要填 sea water，那是它能处理的水源类型，而不是使用它的场所标准；听到 sterile（无菌）时要迅速反应前面的机构。
录音说该设备通过了 hospitals（医院）采用的严格测试标准，以确定水是否足够无菌供其使用。
The present method involves a process called vacuum forming which tends to be rather slow. We’d like to change to an injection mode of process...
不要被后面的 1 million dollars 吓到，那是改变方法所需的成本，不是当前方法的缺点；当前方法的缺点是慢。
录音指出目前的真空成型制造方法有一个问题，就是它往往相当 slow（缓慢）。

There are a number of private companies that are very keen to go into partnership with us over this. What my preferred option would be a global aid agency known as Health International that sponsors projects like ours.
你可能听到 private companies（私营公司），但录音说的是它们很想合作，而演讲者“首选”（preferred option）的是 Health International。
演讲者明确表示，他首选的合作方是一个名为 Health International 的全球援助机构。

However, on a hot day when the temperature is around about 25 to 30 degrees Celsius, with the sun shining clearly through a blue sky, it produces anywhere from 7 liters per day to as much as 9 liters.
题目问的是最大产量（maximum output），所以要填 as much as 后面的数字，不要填 7（最小）或 25 to 30（温度）。
录音提到在晴朗炎热的日子里，该设备每天能生产从7升到多达 9 升的水。
So even under difficult conditions, one family could live off one of these devices. So a normal size village would require several of these to supply all its needs.
不要填 village，录音说一个村庄需要“几台”（several）设备，而题目问的是“每一台”（Each SW40）能满足谁的需求。
录音总结说，即使在困难条件下，一个 family（家庭）也可以靠这一台设备生活。

analyses.content: 录音描述让大自然（阳光）穿过 glass（玻璃）窗/盖子来发挥作用，图中标注的是光线穿过的顶层材质。
You then let mother nature in the form of the sun do its work as it shines through the glass window. It produces infra red light which heats the water.
不要填 lid 或 window，虽然录音都提到了，但 glass 是修饰材质的核心词，也是图中箭头指向的透明面板最准确的描述。
You need an incline so the water flows through the device. The optimum is 12.5 degrees to the horizontal, although it can be 1 or 2 degrees above or below that.
不要填 1 or 2，那是允许的误差范围（above or below）；注意听到 "The optimum is..." 后面紧跟的核心数据。
录音提到水流过设备的最佳角度（optimum）是水平面 12.5 度。
At the same time ultraviolet light from the sun or UV as we more commonly call it is also radiated. If there are germs present in the water, prolonged exposure to this type of light will kill them.
不要填 UV 或 light，图中的箭头如果指向水里的点点，通常是在问“被杀死的对象”；如果是指下来的线，才是光线。此处结合语境 kill them，填 germs。
录音解释说，紫外线（UV）照射会杀死水种存在的 germs（细菌/病菌），图中箭头指向被光线杀死的微小颗粒。
The droplets of water slowly run down the glass to a collection tank, ready to be taken away for drinking or whatever.
只填 tank 也可以得分，但 collection tank 更完整；注意听方位的移动，"run down... to..." 引导出最终归宿。
录音描述水滴顺着玻璃流下，进入一个 collection tank（收集箱/储水箱），对应图中底部的容器。
